parsed.explanation: Trans-specific evidence is essentially absent, so I extrapolate from structure rather than defaulting to the midpoint. Downward: a live (if rarely enforced) sexual-conduct statute carrying years-plus-lashes, extended to all persons in 2014 and applied as recently as a 2015 private-home arrest; no gender-identity non-discrimination protection; official rejection of 60 trans/LGBT-inclusive UPR recommendations; pervasive societal stigma and a taboo rendering the local movement online-only. Upward: no trans-specific offence, border/document/screening rule, facility ban, custody rule or care restriction anywhere in the record; no documented police use of the statute as a lever against gender-nonconforming people; no trans-specific violence figure (the 2013 stabbing is LGB, dated, isolated). Resident-facing items (asylum-on-return, prosecutions of locals, online harassment of activists) do not transfer. The resort carve-out is unverified guidance, not law. Open questions (marker classification at entry, custody/care placement) are unanswered, not exposures. Sits above the 0.35–0.45 tier, which requires documented universal or recurring visitor-facing harm, but below the acceptance-with-minimum-friction tier.
